title: AI-powered DeterTech cameras may have cut trespass at Dingwall's canal level crossings from about five incidents a day in June 2025
summary: Network Rail reported that trespass at Dingwall fell after it installed DeterTech AI cameras alongside signage and campaigns; it gave no later count and noted a renewed rise.
account: Monitoring in June 2025 found an average of five trespass incidents a day at Dingwall, where people used the bridge as a shortcut between the Dingwall Canal North and South crossings. Network Rail then installed AI-powered DeterTech cameras. The cameras detect people leaving the designated route, sound warnings, and send images to Network Rail and British Transport Police. Signage, safety campaigns, and minor site changes accompanied the installation. Network Rail reported on 9 June 2026 that trespass at Dingwall had declined after the installation. The release gives no count after the installation. It says that incidents had begun rising again as the weather improved. It does not isolate the cameras’ effect or document an individual alert that prevented an accident.
purpose: The cameras are built to detect people leaving the designated route, warn them and alert Network Rail and police in real time.
system: DeterTech AI-powered cameras with audio warnings and live image relay
deployer: Network Rail (Scotland's Railway) with British Transport Police
